title: React Interview Questions Applied Check
description: Apply React interview reasoning to tricky hooks, performance, coding challenge, and frontend system design scenarios.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: An interview counter with step uses `setCount(count + step)` inside a delayed callback and sometimes uses old values. What answer should you discuss?

options.text: Stale closures and functional updates or correct dependencies

questions.explanation: Delayed callbacks often expose stale closure problems; functional updates can read the latest state.

questions.prompt: A candidate puts `useEffect` around a calculation that can be derived during render. What is the likely critique?

options.text: Avoid unnecessary effects for derived render data
Derived values must be stored in localStorage

questions.explanation: Interview answers should avoid using effects as a default escape hatch for derived data.

questions.prompt: For a fetch coding challenge, which UI states should usually be represented? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: A hidden failure state with no message

questions.explanation: Fetch challenges should communicate loading, failure, and success clearly.

questions.prompt: A tabs coding challenge keeps active tab by array index, then tabs can be reordered. What is the robust alternative?

options.text: Store active tab in CSS only

questions.explanation: Stable ids preserve identity when collections reorder.

questions.prompt: A modal challenge has no Escape key support and does not restore focus. What topic should you raise?
questions.explanation: Modal implementations are judged on interaction quality as well as rendering.

questions.prompt: A cart reducer mutates the existing item object and returns the same state array. What bug can this cause?

options.text: React may not see a changed reference and UI updates become unreliable

questions.explanation: Reducers should return new references for changed state.

questions.prompt: In a product-page system design interview, the interviewer asks about slow images and reviews loading late. Which answer is strongest?

options.text: Discuss skeletons, progressive loading, caching, layout stability, and failure states
Say React.memo solves all of it
Move all data into props manually

questions.explanation: Good frontend design answers cover network, rendering, and user experience tradeoffs.

questions.prompt: An interviewer asks how to design authentication in a React app. What should be included?

options.text: Auth state loading, protected routes, token/session handling, server enforcement, and logout
Only hiding links in the nav
Only a login form CSS layout

questions.explanation: Authentication design needs state, routing, storage, security, and backend enforcement considerations.
